allocation.question: Now that the mandatory-discovery deterministic REST substrate produced both cold re-derivation and retrieval-shaped comparators at 1.0 correctness ceiling (dynamic range unsatisfiable for the frozen cost/novelty test), can we construct or identify a programmatic, budget-stable, credential-free model endpoint and/or task bank engineered for ASYMMETRIC discovery (multi-task sessions where one-time discovery is amortized/cached across tasks) such that the four-arm C-LLM-INHERIT benchmark (same model/tools/budget: COLD vs INSTRUCTIONS vs RETRIEVAL vs SPIDER, parameterized mechanism carrier bound to git blob b15ed848 / sha256 718efa6a167c2fdc483a8fbaaf1a05ce018dcb1c52808414b2a6a76d788bfb72) produces genuine behavioral variance (COLD success_rate meaningfully below 1.0 ceiling) and treatment/comparator distinction exists? If not provisionable, produce explicit provisioning receipt and do not rerun the mandatory-discovery deterministic REST certificate. Focus on counter-only metrics (http_requests + retrieval_calls + verification_calls + repair_attempts) and novelty-monotonicity. This addresses readiness conditions (2) and (3) before executing expensive LLM-inheritance economics.
allocation.rationale: Product owns external-agent behavior and product economics. The three readiness conditions for expensive C-LLM-INHERIT/C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY/C-PRODUCT-ECON are not satisfied (dynamic range/endpoint missing). Rather than funding full benchmark, Product must remove blockers first. The question targets exactly (2) and (3): create discriminating baselines via asymmetric discovery or alternative substrate, and secure programmatic endpoint prerequisites. This is the highest-leverage action for product claims; it prevents spending cycles on non-discriminating tests.
